title: Guaranteed Serve Obligation: error budget spec, measurement, and contract wording
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: Define a tractable, legally defensible way to promise dedicated serving capacity while preserving operational flexibility. This ticket establishes the 'Guaranteed Serve Obligation' (GSO) construct, an error-budget model, measurement windows, an example credit schedule for contract language, and the operational tie-ins to autoscaling and fleet controls.

Scope and key terminology:
- Guaranteed Serve Obligation (GSO): the contract-level commitment expressed as a sustained throughput entitlement for a customer (tokens/sec or requests/sec) over a rolling measurement window. The GSO replaces ad-hoc phrases like 'throughput SLA' with a single, precise metric family.
- Measurement quantum: per-minute effective serve rate aggregated across the customer's reserved pool and compatible fallbacks.
- Performance cushion: a configurable percentage allowance designed to absorb transient noise without triggering credits.
- Error budget: the aggregate allowable shortfall between the GSO and observed serving rate over the measurement window.

Measurement and math (proposal):
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window with per-minute granularity. Shorter windows (e.g., 7-day) can be used for alerting but not for credit computation.
- Service metric: 1-minute effective serve rate (ESR) measured as the count of successfully started token generations divided by minute. For request-based plans use started requests/minute.
- Availability quantile: compute the 5th percentile (p5) of ESR across the 30-day window. The GSO is considered met for the billing period if p5(ESR) >= 0.95 * GSO_committed after applying Performance Cushion.
- Error budget (EB): EB = max(0, GSO_committed - p5(ESR)) expressed as a percentage of GSO_committed averaged over the window.

Credit calculation example (illustrative):
- Customer GSO_committed: 120,000 tokens/min 
- Performance Cushion: 5% (automatically applied) => effective commitment for measurement = 114,000 tokens/min
- Observed p5(ESR) over 30 days = 100,000 tokens/min
- Shortfall = 14,000 tokens/min => ShortfallPct = 14,000 / 114,000 = 12.28%
- Monthly credit banding (proposed):
  * ShortfallPct <= 2% => 0% credit
  * 2% < ShortfallPct <= 10% => 5% monthly credit
  * 10% < ShortfallPct <= 25% => 15% monthly credit
  * ShortfallPct > 25% => 30% monthly credit (subject to max cap and exclusions)

Contract language guidance (snippet for SOW):
- "Redwood shall provide a Guaranteed Serve Obligation (GSO) equal to the committed serving rate specified in Section X. GSO measurement is based on the 5th percentile per-minute Effective Serve Rate (ESR) across a rolling 30-day window, after application of the contractual Performance Cushion. In the event GSO is not met, Customer will be eligible for service credits computed according to the Shortfall Banding Table in Exhibit A. Service credits are the exclusive remedy for performance shortfalls except for breaches resulting from Redwood gross negligence or willful misconduct."
- Exclusions: planned maintenance announced 72 hours in advance, force majeure, customer-caused throttling or misconfigurations, and documented third-party provider outages.

Operational interplay with autoscaling and fleet controls:
- Autoscaler policy: dedicated pools have two knobs: target_buffer (percent of GSO kept warm) and burst_pool (short-lived scalable capacity). Proposed defaults: target_buffer=10%, burst_pool=25% of GSO.
- Backfill and fallback: when dedicated pool is saturated, requests are routed to customer's compatible fallback model instances (lower-cost or quantized variants) only if customer opt-in is enabled. Redirected traffic counts toward ESR but flagged in telemetry.
- Graceful degradation window: short transient drops (<3m) are ignored for credit computation but trigger on-call paging at higher severity if outside error budget burn rate thresholds.

Telemetry and auditability:
- Primary sources: metric feed 'dedicated.esr.per_minute', route-level traces, and KV cache hit rate. All measurements must be reproducible from raw time-series.
- Audit reports: every monthly credit event will include a reproducible audit bundle (metrics slice, rollup script, and config snapshot) for the customer and legal review.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Product spec + legal contract snippets drafted and reviewed by Legal.
2) Measurement algorithm implemented in telemetry back-end with a public QA dashboard showing p5(ESR) over 30 days.
3) Credit calculator utility (internal) that consumes the metric slice and emits a proposed credit percent with reproducible evidence.
4) Autoscaler defaults implemented and linked to the GSO knobs; unit tests and a canary exercise completed.
5) Runbook for on-call and remediation steps documented and validated against a simulated degradation incident.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Choosing p5 vs p1 or p10 affects sensitivity to outliers; p5 chosen as a balance between transient noise and meaningful customer experience.
- Rolling 30-day windows smooth variability but delay detection of regressions; separate alerting windows mitigate this.
- Credit bands must be conservative enough to protect customers but capped to manage financial exposure.

Next steps and owners:
- Legal: review exclusion language and maximum credit cap (owner: Asha Patel, due 2025-02-07)
- Engineering telemetry: implement reproducible p5 calculation (owner: Eric Zhou, due 2025-02-14)
- Runtime: implement autoscaler knobs and burst_pool (owner: Priya Nair, due 2025-02-21)
- Docs/Console: create QA dashboard and audit bundle flow (owner: Mateo Ruiz, due 2025-03-01)
comments: 2025-01-20 — Asha Patel: Legal flagged need for explicit caps on aggregate monthly credits and a 'good faith' reconciliation clause.

2025-01-22 — Eric Zhou: Telemetry can emit per-minute ESR using the existing generation-start metric; will add a p5 rollup job in metrics pipeline. Investigating corners where fallback routing inflates ESR while hiding customer experience degradation.

2025-01-28 — Priya Nair: Runtime team proposes autoscaler default of target_buffer=10% and burst_pool=25%. Concern: burst_pool non-determinism could make credits noisy; suggest isolating burst usage from credit computation by labeling metrics.
2025-02-03 — Legal: Requested explicit exclusion language for maintenance windows and an operational notice process; asked PM to add 72-hour notice language.
2025-02-10 — Design (Mateo Ruiz): Dashboard mockups uploaded to Confluence; includes p5 chart, shortfall percentile heatmap, and downloadable audit bundle button.
2025-02-20 — Sofia Martinez: Updated credit bands based on finance feedback to limit worst-case exposure. Ready for engineering ETA confirmation.

acceptance_criteria: Legal has approved Exhibit A credit banding and exclusion clauses
Telemetry pipeline emits a reproducible p5(ESR) computation for any 30-day slice
Internal credit calculator outputs match manual audit in 3 representative customer slices
Autoscaler knobs are configurable per-customer and default values are documented
Console displays a downloadable audit bundle for any creditable month
decision_log: Decision 2025-01-18: Use rolling 30-day window and p5 quantile for credit computation (tradeoff: smoothing vs detection latency).
Decision 2025-01-28: Performance Cushion default set to 5% to reduce noisy credits for transient spikes.
Decision 2025-02-14: Burst pool usage will be labeled and excluded from credit calculation unless customer explicit opt-in is set.
Decision 2025-02-21: Credit banding tiers agreed with Finance; cap on monthly credits set to 30% pending final legal review.
